notes:
The two passes agree on every requirement, row, id, cell and disposition (eight checks kept, the notification check weak); their texts and assumptions differ in wording only. One wrote the active cells on the skill and the rule as the predicate '= true', the other as the plain value true; the two are the same test, and the plain value is kept.
The acting user, Joanne Simpson, holds the manager role; the policy says managers cannot modify system configuration and lists assignment rules among the administrator's tables, so creating the skill and the rule could be refused under a strict reading. The file follows the request and the benchmark, which both expect every step done; a strict reading would turn the skill and assignment-rule requirements into stays. The case is awaiting_approval on the seed; the request asks for no status change, so status is not tested. The case's skills column (JSON) is null on every seed case, so its storage format is not shown and no cell is written for it. The policy's short-description format (Service, Subject, Detail) and its 30-120 character limit are not tested by the benchmark and are left out. The case checks' number predicate is dropped because the anchor hr_case_id 21 names the same row. The combined check is a conjunction of the other checks and is carried jointly by every requirement; its notification part holds on the seed, but the whole does not.
